subject: Questions about configuring MCMC for returned samples and summary stats

messages.author: 4a248770402c04bc
messages.subject: Questions about configuring MCMC for returned samples and summary stats
parts:
In the model I'm working with, there is a small set of nodes for which I want the full MCMC chains. There is a large set of nodes for which I would like summary statistics, but no chains. This leads me to several questions.
  • When configuring MCMC, are the options `summary` and `samples` global or can they be set for individual nodes?
  • Is the set of summary statistics invariable or can it be specified?
  • Is thinning performed before or after summary statistics are calculated?
Cheers,
Gregory

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Questions about configuring MCMC for returned samples and summary stats
parts:
Are you asking about configureMCMC (which we think of as the configuration step, but it lacks "summary" and "samples" options) or compareMCMCs, which now lives here: https://github.com/nimble-dev/compareMCMCs

The User Manual / vignette linked from the compareMCMCs github page shows how to include a new summary statistic (a "metric").  IIRC, thinning is done before the metric is calculated.  Choice of summaries/metrics is not currently splittable by nodes.

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Questions about configuring MCMC for returned samples and summary stats
parts:
Got it.  Back to your original questions then: no, the "samples" and "summary" are intimately connected.  You cannot get "summary statistics" for nodes which are not monitored (have samples recorded) by the MCMC.  So if you want summary statistics for your (large number of) deterministic nodes, you'll have to monitor those deterministic nodes.

The set of "summary statistics" is really just a post-processing step performed on the recorded samples.  The statistics could be modified if need be; but I think the bigger answer is that you'd have to ask the MCMC to monitor all your deterministic nodes, in order to calculate summary statistics for them, regardless of whether you ask the MCMC to return the samples to you.

Last: summary statistics are calculated using the post-thinning samples (since those are the only ones recorded by the MCMC, hence they are the ones used to calculate summary statistics).

Does that answer your questions?

Fantastic.  I like the idea a lot, and will consider it as a future addition to the MCMC.  The short answer, is that (within reason) anything is possible, and it's just a matter of implementing it.  A feature like this (perhaps called "accumulators" ?) could be made available through the lowest-level invocation of the MCMC, specifically, using mcmc$run().

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Questions about configuring MCMC for returned samples and summary stats
parts:
Hi Gregory,

As an immediate option if you want to accomplish your goal, if you are game to modify a nimbleFunction, you can do the following:

Go to nimble source code, R/MCMC_build.R (https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/blob/master/packages/nimble/R/MCMC_build.R).  This is the nimbleFunction for an MCMC.  It manages calling the list of samplers and collecting outputs.

Make a local copy of this nimbleFunction and insert what you want in the master loop, starting at line 188.  The nimCopy lines are where samples for monitors are saved in the mvSamples (output).

If you want an accumulator to be available afterward, create it first in the setup code.  Example:

In setup code:
myAccumulator <- 0

In run code, in the master loop, do whatever accumulation step(s) you need, like:
myAccumulator <- myAccumulator + model$x[1] ## or whatever

Then, after you build the MCMC, you will be able to access myAccumulator as
MCMC$myAccumulator
in either the compiled or uncompiled version.

You can add getter and setter methods for myAccumulator if it helps.

If you need myAccumulator to be a vector, it is important to create it in setup code with length > 1 so the compiler knows for sure it is a vector:
myAccumulator <- c(0, 0)

Then use your local version of buildMCMC instead of the package version.

HTH
Perry

Great.  While you're "thinking about [the set of accumulators] and coming back", let me add another question for you:

In your mind, would the specific values accumulated (getting added together) be tied to the thinning interval?  That is, if thin=10, we only "add up" every 10th sample -- even if we're not *recording* (monitoring) the samples?  This would be more natural in terms of implementation, and also more obvious regarding the question "how many samples were accumulated?, that is, how many did we add together?", since it's the same number as the number of rows in the samples array.

That said, since accumulators wouldn't actually be tied intimately to the monitors (that's the idea, right), it perhaps would make more sense to add together *all* samples, regardless of thinning (this begs a further question: what about pre-burn-in samples?).  In the case of accumulating every sample, regardless of whatever thinning is taking place for the monitored samples, I'd perhaps also maintain another variable, simply giving the "number of samples that were accumulated, in the cumulative sum", so that the answer to the question "how many samples were accumulated" is obvious and transparent.

Your thoughts, Gregory, are welcomed.

For example, I'd like to estimate the mean and variance of those nodes using something like Welford's online algorithm. It seems like this would not break the concept of a monitor as something that is triggered when a node is updated, and then does something, like store the new value in a data structure or use the new value to perform some calculation and then discard it, or anything else.

Cheers,
Gregory

On Tuesday, November 19, 2019 at 3:27:52 PM UTC-7, Daniel Turek wrote:
Got it.  Back to your original questions then: no, the "samples" and "summary" are intimately connected.  You cannot get "summary statistics" for nodes which are not monitored (have samples recorded) by the MCMC.  So if you want summary statistics for your (large number of) deterministic nodes, you'll have to monitor those deterministic nodes.

The set of "summary statistics" is really just a post-processing step performed on the recorded samples.  The statistics could be modified if need be; but I think the bigger answer is that you'd have to ask the MCMC to monitor all your deterministic nodes, in order to calculate summary statistics for them, regardless of whether you ask the MCMC to return the samples to you.

Last: summary statistics are calculated using the post-thinning samples (since those are the only ones recorded by the MCMC, hence they are the ones used to calculate summary statistics).

Does that answer your questions?


On Tue, Nov 19, 2019 at 9:10 PM Gregory Penn <grego...@gmail.com> wrote:
I was asking about configureMCMC. I'll look at compareMCMCs and see whether that'll do what I'm looking for. Essentially, I have a large number of deterministic nodes for which I'd like to have summary statistics. I can calculate those from the MCMC chains for stochastic notes, so it would just be a convenience to have the summaries accumulated by the model. I haven't looked at the C++ code side of Nimble, but I was thinking that it might use Boost Accumulators for summaries, which would provide a lot of adaptability.

Gregory

On Saturday, November 16, 2019 at 1:45:55 PM UTC-7, pdevalpine wrote:
Are you asking about configureMCMC (which we think of as the configuration step, but it lacks "summary" and "samples" options) or compareMCMCs, which now lives here: https://github.com/nimble-dev/compareMCMCs

The User Manual / vignette linked from the compareMCMCs github page shows how to include a new summary statistic (a "metric").  IIRC, thinning is done before the metric is calculated.  Choice of summaries/metrics is not currently splittable by nodes.





On Sat, Nov 16, 2019 at 11:51 AM Gregory Penn <grego...@gmail.com> wrote:
In the model I'm working with, there is a small set of nodes for which I want the full MCMC chains. There is a large set of nodes for which I would like summary statistics, but no chains. This leads me to several questions.
  • When configuring MCMC, are the options `summary` and `samples` global or can they be set for individual nodes?
  • Is the set of summary statistics invariable or can it be specified?
  • Is thinning performed before or after summary statistics are calculated?
Cheers,
Gregory

messages.subject: Re: Questions about configuring MCMC for returned samples and summary stats
parts:
Greg, I've implemented essentially this functionality on a developmental branch of the nimble package, called "accumulators".  You can install the modified package from that branch using the R code:

remove.packages("nimble")
library(devtools)
install_github("nimble-dev/nimble", ref = "accumulators", subdir = "packages/nimble")
library(nimble)

Below I'll copy a snippet from the documentation that I wrote, which should explain the usage of accumulators well enough.  Let me know if you give it a try, have any problems, or suggestions.

Cheers!
Daniel


Accumulators can be used to calculate the cumulative sum, and sum-of-squares, for an arbitrary set of model variables during the course of MCMC sampling.  These accumulated values can subsequently be accessed and used to calculate posterior mean and posterior standard deviation, even when monitors are not assigned, and therefore samples are not recorded, for model variables.  Accumulator values are cumulatively summed regardless of any thinning or burn-in (which only affect the posterior samples recorded).

Accumulator variables must be specified in the MCMC configuration object, using either the \code{setAccumulators} method of the MCMC configuration object as \code{conf$setAccumulators('x', 'y')}, or via the \code{accumulators} argument to \code{configureMCMC} as \code{conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, accumulators = c('x', 'y'))}.  Accumulator variables can be reset using \code{conf$resetAccumulators()}.

After running an MCMC algorithm, a matrix containing the cumulative sums, and sums-of-squares, for the specified variables can be retrieved using \code{as.matrix(mcmc$mvAccumulators)}.  The first row of this matrix contains the cumulative sums, and the second row contains the cumulative sums-of-squares.  The total number of summed values (resulting from that many MCMC iterations) can be retrieved using the \code{getAccumulatorIterations} method of the MCMC object, as \code{mcmc$getAccumulatorIterations()}.

On Mon, Nov 25, 2019 at 8:28 AM Daniel Turek <db...@williams.edu> wrote:
Great.  While you're "thinking about [the set of accumulators] and coming back", let me add another question for you:

In your mind, would the specific values accumulated (getting added together) be tied to the thinning interval?  That is, if thin=10, we only "add up" every 10th sample -- even if we're not *recording* (monitoring) the samples?  This would be more natural in terms of implementation, and also more obvious regarding the question "how many samples were accumulated?, that is, how many did we add together?", since it's the same number as the number of rows in the samples array.

That said, since accumulators wouldn't actually be tied intimately to the monitors (that's the idea, right), it perhaps would make more sense to add together *all* samples, regardless of thinning (this begs a further question: what about pre-burn-in samples?).  In the case of accumulating every sample, regardless of whatever thinning is taking place for the monitored samples, I'd perhaps also maintain another variable, simply giving the "number of samples that were accumulated, in the cumulative sum", so that the answer to the question "how many samples were accumulated" is obvious and transparent.

Your thoughts, Gregory, are welcomed.


On Sun, Nov 24, 2019 at 7:21 PM Gregory Penn <gregor...@gmail.com> wrote:
I'm sure there is a limited set of accumulators that would cover most use cases. I'll think about what that set might look like and come back here with that, but the running total sum and sum of squares would clearly be the place to start. Right now my mind is on moving my Nimble work off my laptop and onto a SLURM managed cluster, about which I'll be posting questions soon.

Cheers,
Gregory

On Thursday, November 21, 2019 at 4:37:45 AM UTC-7, Daniel Turek wrote:
Fantastic.  I like the idea a lot, and will consider it as a future addition to the MCMC.  The short answer, is that (within reason) anything is possible, and it's just a matter of implementing it.  A feature like this (perhaps called "accumulators" ?) could be made available through the lowest-level invocation of the MCMC, specifically, using mcmc$run().

Without having looked at the reference you sent, just one quick question - would the only "accumulators" we'd be interested in, perhaps, be "running total sum", and "running total sum of squares"?  I ask, because (1) I think those would be sufficient for calculating mean and variance, as you suggest, and (2) from an implementation standpoint, it would be a lot simpler if the only types of "accumulators" allowed were restricted to those two (fixed, predefined, and finite-in-number) types.  It would be a lot more (implementation) effort to allow for fully general "accumulators", e.g., "sum of log-logs", or whatever otherwise.
